ForceAbility.Name: Alter Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The basic power of Alter allows the user to tap into the Living Force of their surroundings, manipulating the nearby environs. The basic power has two uses, both of which can only be used in natural terrain that can change form easily, such as dirt, sand, mud, and thick vegetation. [BR]- The Force user may spend a Force point to make all terrain currently within short range difficult terrain until the end of their next turn. The Force user must be touching the ground to manifest this power. The user may not activate this multiple times. [BR]- The Force user may spend a Force point to make all terrain currently within short range normal terrain until the end of their next turn. The Force user must be touching the ground to manifest this power. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Battle Meditation Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: Battle Meditation's basic power allows the Force user to influence and coordinate large groups of allies, guiding their actions to help them work as a unified whole. The basic power has one way of spending Force points:[P]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to add one automatic success result to all checks made by a number of engaged friendly targets up to the user's Presence before the end of their next turn. If the user uses any Dark points to generate Force points ([FORCEPOINT]) on this check, reduce each target's Willpower by 1 (to a minimum of 1) until the end of the encounter. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Bind Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: Bind's basic power allows the Force user to restrain those nearby, preventing them from harming others and themselves. The basic power has one way to spend Force points: [BR]- The user may spend a Force point to immobilize a target within short range until the end of the user's next turn. If the user used any Dark points to generate Force points on this check, the target also suffers 1 wound (ignoring soak) per Force point spent on the check. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Conjure Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The basic power of Conjure allows the user to create an approximation of a close-combat weapon or other small object using the Force, which lasts for a short time before ceasing to exist. The power has one basic effect. [BR]- The Force user may spend a Force point to create a facsimile of a Brawl or Melee weapon with the following profile: (Brawl or Melee; Damage +3; Critical 3; Range Engaged; Cortosis). This item appears anywhere within short range of the user. The item functions as normal, but at the end of the user's next turn, the item dissipates. If the item is moved beyond short range from the Force user, it also immediately dissipates. At the GM's discretion, the user can also conjure a simple tool or other useful low-tech item that has an encumbrance of no greater than one this way. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control - Additional Injuries
ForceAbility.Description: The character can commit additional Force dice to temporarily ignore one additional Critical Injury per Control upgrade purchased.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Initiative
ForceAbility.Description: When performing a Warde's Foresight power check as part of an Initiative check, the user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to add an automatic [ADVANTAGE] result to the first check they make this encounter (after the Initiative check). The user may activate this multiple times, adding additional automatic [ADVANTAGE] results to the check each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Agility
ForceAbility.Description: This power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. The Force user increases their Agility characteristic by 1 (to a maximum of 6).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: All Attacks/Ensnare
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Protect and for Unleash.[P]- [B]Protect:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to have the barrier protect against all types of attacks instead of only protecting against energy attacks. The user may not activate this multiple times. [BR]- [B]Unleash:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to have the attack gain the Ensnare 2 quality. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Ally Initiative
ForceAbility.Description: When performing a Warde's Foresight power check as part of an Initiative check, if the user did not use a Dark point to generate Force points ([FORCEPOINT]), each ally adds an automatic success result to the results of their Initiative check. If the user used a Dark point to generate Force points ([FORCEPOINT]), the user may immediately perform an action before the encounter begins, but each enemy in the encounter adds an automatic success result to the results of their Initiative check.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Animal Senses
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to share the senses of non-sentient animals and similar creatures within range of their power. The Force user adds a [BOOST] die to Perception and Vigilance checks, and at the GM's discretion, may be able to learn or notice things they could not normally perceive. This lasts for the duration of the power. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Appearance
ForceAbility.Description: Instead of merely hiding an object or person from the target with this power, the user may alter the appearance of that object or person, making it appear to be something or someone else to the target.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Brawl
ForceAbility.Description: Enhance can be used with the Brawl skill.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Brawn
ForceAbility.Description: This power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. The Force user increases their Brawn characteristic by 1 (to a maximum of 6).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Combat
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user gains the ability to blur their own form in the eyes of others, causing their attacks to miss vital spots and creating excellent opportunities for their own counterblows. The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit one or more Force dice: Add an automatic [THREAT] result per Force die committed to all combat checks made against the Force user.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Commit
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit one or more Force dice: When an opponent targets the user with a Force power, after the opponent generates Force points ([FORCEPOINT]), reduce the total Force points ([FORCEPOINT]) generated by 1 per Force die committed, to a minimum of 0.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Concealment
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to give all characters within short range of the Force user concealment, adding a [SETBACK] die or [BOOST] die to appropriate checks. This lasts for the duration of the power. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Coordination
ForceAbility.Description: The user gains the ability to use Enhance with the Coordination skill.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Corrosive Atmosphere
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend two Force points to create a corrosive atmosphere in a small area within the power's area of effect. This area is no more than 3 meters across. The rating of the corrosive atmosphere is equal to the user's current Force rating. This lasts for the duration of the power. The user may activate this multiple times, choosing a new patch of terrain to affect each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Critical
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Heal and for Harm.[P]- [B]Heal:[b] When the user is making a [B]Heal power check[b], they may also roll a [B]Hard difficulty Medicine check[b] as part of the pool. If they heal one or more wounds on a target and succeeds on the Medicine check, they may also heal one Critical Injury that target is suffering. [BR]- [B]Harm:[b] When the Force user is making a [B]Harm power check[b], they may also roll an [B]opposed Medicine versus Resilience check[b] (if the check was not already opposed) as part of the pool. If they inflict one or more wounds on a target and succeeds on the Medicine check, they may also inflict one Critical Injury on the target and may spend two [ADVANTAGE] results to add +10 to the roll (they may spend two [ADVANTAGE] results to increase the roll multiple times).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Defense
ForceAbility.Description: When performing a Foresee power check as part of an Initiative check, all targets affected by the power increase their ranged and melee defense by 2 for the first round of combat.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Defense Qualities
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user gains the ability to imbue a created weapon with certain defensive qualities, which might manifest around the item as a blurred protective aura, a form that twists and shifts to protect the wielder, or a halo of crackling energy. Spend a Force point to grant one conjured weapon one of the following qualities: Defensive 1, Deflection 1, or Stun 4. The user can activate this multiple times, granting the weapon an additional quality each time (but may not grant the same quality more than once).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Defense/Strain
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Protect and for Unleash.[P]- [B]Protect:[b] The user may spend [ADVANTAGE] results to gain ranged and melee defense equal to the [ADVANTAGE] results spent until the beginning of the their next turn. [BR]- [B]Unleash:[b] The user may spend an [ADVANTAGE] result on their Discipline check to inflict 1 strain on the target (ignoring soak).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Destiny
ForceAbility.Description: Once per game session, the Force user may spend a Destiny Point to use Suppress as an out of turn incidental.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Emotion/Belief

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: To gain the ability to alter the thoughts and emotions of a living target with whom they are engaged, the user makes an [B]opposed Discipline check[b] against the target as part of the pool to activate the power. The user must spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) [I]and[i] they must succeed on the check to force the target to adopt an emotional state such as fear, friendliness, or hatred, or to believe something untrue ("these are not the droids you are looking for"). The effect lasts for roughly five minutes, or one round of combat. If the Force user has the ability to affect multiple minds with this power (such as with the Magnitude upgrade), the Discipline check either must be opposed by the mind with the highest ranks in Discipline, or its difficulty must be set statically based on the number of minds (at the GM's discretion).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Failure/Success
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Ebb and Flow.[P]- [B]Ebb:[b] When making a combined Ebb power check, the Force user may spend a Force point to add a [FAILURE] result to all checks made by engaged opponents until the end of the Force user's next turn. The Force user may not activate this multiple times. [BR]- [B]Flow:[b] When making a combined Flow power check, the Force user may spend a Force point to add a success to any checks the Force user makes that use the same skill before the end of the user's next turn. The Force user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Fine Details
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to make out fine details on one object within medium range. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of objects by one each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Firm Terrain
ForceAbility.Description: This power can affect firm natural terrain, such as packed earth, stone, or ice.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Force Leap (Horizontal)
ForceAbility.Description: The user can take a Force Leap action to make an [B]Enhance power check[b]. They may spend a Force point to jump horizontally to any location within short range. They can use this to leap over obstacles or impassible terrain but cannot leap directly vertically. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Force Leap (Maneuver)
ForceAbility.Description: The user only needs to use a maneuver to perform a Force Leap, instead of an action.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Force Leap (Vertical)
ForceAbility.Description: When taking a Force leap action, the user can leap to any location in range vertically as well as horizontally.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Heal Droid
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point to heal a number of wounds equal to their Intellect in an engaged droid. This counts as the use of an Emergency Repair Patch. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Hurl

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user gains the ability to move objects fast enough so as to be both difficult to dodge and capable of inflicting damage. Resulting impacts deal damage to both the target and the object being moved. The user makes a Force power check and rolls a ranged attack as part of the pool. (This attack uses the Discipline skill.) The attack's difficulty is equal to the silhouette of the object being thrown instead of the normal difficulty for ranged attacks, and only succeeds if the user can also spend enough Force points ([FORCEPOINT]) to move the object. Silhouette 0 objects deal 5 damage, while other objects deal damage equal to ten times their silhouette. The number of targets affected by a single object is up to the GM, but in general, a single object should only affect a single target, unless the object is particularly large. If the player wants to use multiple objects to hit multiple targets, they may do so by using the rules for hitting multiple targets with the Auto-fire quality. This attack follows all the rules for ranged attacks, including ranged defense and aiming.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Illusion
ForceAbility.Description: Instead of hiding an object or person from the target with this power, the user may cause the target to see a vision of an illusory object, person, or creature where none exists. This phantasm can be silhouette 1 or smaller. To accomplish this, the Force user may also roll an [B]opposed Deception versus Vigilance check[b] (if the check was not already opposed) as part of the pool. To make the target experience the illusion, the user must generate enough Force points ([FORCEPOINT]) to create the illusion [I]and[i] must succeed at the opposed check. If the user spent any Dark points to generate a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]), each target subjected to the unsettling illusion suffers 1 strain per Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) spent on the check.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Impassible Terrain
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend two Force points to make a small patch of terrain within the power's area of effect impassable terrain. This patch is no more than 3 meters across. The nature of the impassible terrain is up to the Force user; it could be a mass of solid rock, an impenetrable morass of twisting underbrush, or a bubbling pit of steam and superheated water. This lasts for the duration of the power. The user may activate this multiple times, choosing a new patch of terrain to affect each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Incidental/Maneuver
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Protect and for Unleash.[P]- [B]Protect[b]: If they are a light side Force user, then once per game session, the user may spend a Destiny Point to use Protect as an out-of-turn incidental. [BR]- [B]Unleash[b]: If they are a dark side Force user, then once per game session, the Force user may spend a Destiny Point to use Unleash as a maneuver.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Increase Hull Trauma
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit one or more Force dice. Increase the hull trauma threshold of one vehicle or starship at engaged range by 3 per Force die committed.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Increase System Strain
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit one or more Force dice. Increase the system strain threshold of one vehicle or starship at engaged range by 3 per Force die committed.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Inflict Strain
ForceAbility.Description: When performing a combat check against a droid, ship, vehicle, or other mechanical construct within engaged range, the user may spend a Force point to inflict 1 additional strain or system strain on the target. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the strain or system strain inflicted by one each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Initiative (Maneuver)
ForceAbility.Description: When performing a Foresee power check as part of an Initiative check, the user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to allow all affected targets to take one free maneuver before the first round of combat begins. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Initiative (Success)
ForceAbility.Description: When making a skill check to determine Initiative, the user may roll a [B]Foresee power check[b] as part of the pool. They may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to gain a success result on their check, and may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Item Damage
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. One damaged weapon or item counts as being undamaged. This can be activated multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Maneuver
ForceAbility.Description: Once per encounter, the user may use the basic power as a maneuver.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Manipulate

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user gains the ability to perform fine manipulation of items, allowing them to do whatever they could normally do with their hands to a held item. If this power is used to manipulate something such as a control board, the controls count as an object of silhouette 0.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Mechanics
ForceAbility.Description: When making a Mechanics skill check, the user may roll a Manipulate power check as part of the pool. The user may spend a Force point to gain a success or [ADVANTAGE] result (user's choice) on the check. The user may activate this multiple times, adding additional success or [ADVANTAGE] results to the check each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Medicine
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Heal and for Harm.[P]- [B]Heal:[b] The user increases the number of wounds healed by this power by their ranks in Medicine. [BR]- [B]Harm:[b] The user increases the number of wounds inflicted by this power by their ranks in Medicine.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Microscopic Details
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to see microscopic details of one object within engaged range. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of objects by one ach time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Move
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to immediately move the target one range band toward or away from the user. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Offense Qualities
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user gains the ability to imbue a created weapon with certain offensive qualities that might manifest as a palpable darkness around the item, a keening wail whenever the weapon is swung, or ethereal green flames. Spend a Force point to grant one conjured weapon one of the following qualities: Burn 3, Pierce 3, or Vicious 3. The user can activate this multiple times, granting the weapon an additional quality each time (but not may not grant the same quality more than once).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Orders
ForceAbility.Description: When making a [B]Battle Meditation power check[b], the user may make an [B]Easy difficulty Leadership check[b] as part of the pool. If they generate enough Force points to activate the power and succeed on the check, they can telepathically transmit a simple order to each character they affect with this power. This order is not mandatory, but the recipient comprehends it even if they do not understand the user's languages.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Panoramic Vision
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend two Force points to see in every direction simultaneously, noticing and observing things in a full 360-degree arc. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Perception
ForceAbility.Description: This power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. The Force user's rank in the Perception skill by 1 (to a maximum of 5) each time this is performed.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Pierce
ForceAbility.Description: As it encompasses the lives of all things, so too does the Force contain the secrets of all ends. From time to time, a particularly perceptive Force user can spot these fault lines in the universe and, in doing so, uncover a unique opportunity or even an opponent's fatal flaw. To a Force user who has honed such an ability, all vulnerabilities and cracks in even the thickest armor are laid bare. The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit three Force dice. The user's attacks gain Pierce with a rating equal to the user's Cunning plus ranks in Perception (or increases existing Pierce rating by the same amount).

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Piloting - Planetary
ForceAbility.Description: Enhance can be used with the Piloting (Planetary) skill.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Piloting - Space
ForceAbility.Description: Enhance can be used with the Piloting (Space) skill.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Planetary Scale
ForceAbility.Description: Before attempting to activate this power, the user may suffer 4 strain to change the range of the Battle Meditation basic power to close on the planetary scale rather than engaged on the personal scale, for this use of the power only. If they do so, activating the range upgrades increases the range of the power by planetary scale range bands.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Pull

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user gains the ability to pull objects off secure mountings or from an opponent's grasp.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Question
ForceAbility.Description: The Force power gains the following effect: Once per encounter, spend three Force points to ask a single "yes-or-no" question pertaining to the current events of the game. The GM must answer truthfully (although depending on how the question is phrased, the answer still may be misleading!)

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Resilience
ForceAbility.Description: Enhance can be used with the Resilience skill.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Sense Thoughts

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user gains the ability to detect the surface thoughts of the target. This power gains the effect: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]). The user senses the current thoughts of one living target with whom they are engaged. The user may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Skill Checks
ForceAbility.Description: The Force power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die until the end of the current encounter. For the remainder of the current encounter, the Force user must add a Force die to all skill checks they make. Each light point and dark point result rolled adds either a success result or [ADVANTAGE] result to the check (the user's choice). However, for each dark point result rolled, the user suffers 1 strain and gains 1 Conflict.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Skill Ranks
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to allow the target to count as having ranks in a single skill equal to the ranks the Force user has in that skill while the target is affected by this power. The skill must be linked to the characteristic improved by this power.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Skills

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user gains the ability to enhance their arguments and charisma via the Force. When making a Coercion, Charm, Deception, Leadership, or Negotiation check, the user may roll an [B]Influence power check[b] as part of the pool. They may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to gain a success result or [ADVANTAGE] result (their choice) per point on the check.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Skills
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user becomes increasingly attuned to the subtle cues in the world around them and is capable of sharpening their mind-senses to cut through all distractions that might conceal important details. The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. Upgrade the ability of all Perception and Vigilance checks the user makes once. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Status
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Heal and for Harm.[P]- [B]Heal:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to immediately remove the staggered, immobilized, or disoriented condition from one target of the power. The user may activate this upgrade multiple times. [BR]- [B]Harm:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to heal a number of wounds on an engaged living creature (including themself) equal to the damage they inflicted on one target. This counts as a use of a stimpack on the target of the healing. The character healed this way gains 1 Conflict. The user may activate this upgrade multiple times, but must select a different target to be healed each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Strain
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point; whenever a target affected by Bind takes an action, they suffer strain equal to the user's Willpower. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Strain
ForceAbility.Description: This Control upgrade has different effects for Heal and for Harm.[P]- [B]Heal:[b] If the user used no Dark points to generate a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) on the check, the target of Heal also heals an amount of strain equal to the wounds they recovered. [BR]- [B]Harm:[b] If the user used any Dark points to generate a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) the check, the user heals of an amount of strain equal to the wounds they inflicted on one target.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Strain
ForceAbility.Description: Whenever an enemy targets a character affected by Suppress with a hostile Force power, if that enemy used any Dark Point to generate Force points ([FORCEPOINT]) on the check, the enemy suffers strain equal to the user's rank of Discipline.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Successes
ForceAbility.Description: When making a skill check to determine Initiative, the Force user may roll a Warde's Foresight power check as part of the pool. They may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to add an automatic success result to the first check they make this encounter (after the Initiative check). The user may activate this multiple times, adding additional automatic success results to the check each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Survival
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to make an [B]Average difficulty Survival check[b]. Success allows the Force user to locate food, water, and other critical supplies within extreme range. In some cases, the GM may determine that there are no such supplies available (for example, if the Force user is on the surface of an airless moon). The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Target
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to track up to one additional target when using this power. The user can activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Threat/Advantage
ForceAbility.Description: This control upgrade has different effects for Ebb and Flow. [BR]- [B]Ebb:[b] When making a combined Ebb power check, the Force user may spend a Force point to add a [THREAT] result to all checks made by engaged opponents until the end of the Force user's next turn. The Force user may not activate this multiple times. [BR]- [B]Flow:[b] When making a combined Flow power check, the Force user may spend a Force point to add an [ADVANTAGE] result to any checks the Force user makes that use the same skill before the end of their next turn. The Force user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Transparent
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point to see through one object at medium range as though it were transparent. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of objects by one each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Upgrade Ability

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The Force user's ability to anticipate danger allows them to anticipate the actions of their opponents while they take the offensive, making their own blows harder to avoid. This power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. Once per round, when the Force user makes a combat check, they upgrade the ability of the pool once. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Upgrade Computers and Mechanics
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. Upgrade the ability of Computers and Mechanics checks once. This cannot be activated multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Upgrade Difficulty
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend two Force points to upgrade the difficulty of all checks made by opponents while in the power's area of effect once. This lasts for the duration of the power.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Upgrade Difficulty

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user gains the ability to sense danger the moment before it strikes, allowing them to anticipate attacks and avoid incoming blows. This power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die. Once per round, when an attack targets the Force user, they upgrade the difficulty of the pool once. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Control: Vigilance
ForceAbility.Description: When making a Vigilance or Perception check, the user may roll a Farsight power check as part of the pool. The user may spend a Force point to gain a success or [ADVANTAGE] result (character's choice) on the check.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die after successfully activating the basic power to sustain its effects as long as the user remains in the area affected.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit three Force dice after successfully activating the basic power. This power remains in effect on each affected target as long as the target stays within range of the power. If a target moves beyond the range of the power, the effects end for them, but not for any other targets of the power. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit three Force dice after successfully activating the basic power. If a target was immobilized or staggered by this power, they remain immobilized or staggered as long as three Force dice remain committed and the target stays within range. If a target moves beyond the range of the power, the effects end for that target, but not for any other targets of the power. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die after successfully activating this power. One conjured facsimile per Duration upgrade purchased remains in existence as long as it stays within short range of the user. If the facsimile moves beyond short range of the user, it ceases to exist.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: As an incidental, the character can activate Endure to affect a Critical Injury the character is already suffering. The character commits a Force die and ignores all effects of the Critical Injury while the Force die remains committed, just as if the power were activated upon first receiving the injury. The Critical Injury must be of a severity that Endure could affect normally.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point to increase the duration by a number of rounds (or minutes in narrative time) equal to Duration upgrades purchased.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to see a number of extra days into the future equal to the number of Duration upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of days by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: After using this power, the Force user may commit two Force dice to sustain the effects of this power as long as the target remains in range.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: After using this power, the Force user may commit a Force die to sustain the effects of this power as long as the target remains in range (instead of two Force dice).

ForceAbility.Name: Duration

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the time this effect lasts by a number of minutes or rounds in combat equal to the number of Duration upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the duration multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: Force users skilled in fooling the senses of others can extend the effects of the ability, shrouding themselves or creating phantasms that last as long as they need such diversions. The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit two Force dice after successfully activating the basic power. This power remains in effect on each affected target as long as the target stays within range of the power. If a target moves beyond the range of the power, the effects end for them but not for any other targets of the power.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The Duration upgrade has different effects for Protect and for Unleash.[P]- [B]Protect:[b] If not Dark points were used to generate a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]), the Force barrier protecting the user's target shields against all energy attacks the target would otherwise suffer before the beginning of the user's next turn (instead of just the next energy attack). [BR]- [B]Unleash:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to give the attack the Burn 2 quality. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die after successfully activating the basic power to find the direction of a person or object. Whenever the person or object moves, the Force user becomes aware of this movement and of the person or object's new general location or the direction they must follow to reach it.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: Sense's ongoing effects may be triggered one additional time per round.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: The power gains the ongoing effect: Commit a Force die after successfully activating the basic power. This power remains in effect on each affected target as long as the target stays within range of the power. If target moves beyond the range of the power, the effects end for them but not for any other targets affected by the power. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Duration
ForceAbility.Description: Spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to have the bonuses granted by this power apply to all relevant checks for a number of rounds equal to the number of Duration upgrades purchased. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Ebb/Flow Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The basic power can be used either to empower the user or to sap strength from the user's foes. The basic power has two ways to spend Force Points. [BR]- [B]Ebb:[b] When the Force user makes a skill check, they may roll an [B]Ebb power check[b] as part of the roll. The user may spend a Force point to suffer 1 strain, then inflict 1 strain on all other engaged characters. The Force user may not activate this multiple times. [BR]- [B]Flow:[b] When the Force user makes a skill check, they may roll a [B]Flow power check[b] as part of the roll. The user may spend a Force point to heal 1 strain. The Force user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Endure Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The basic power of Endure allows a Force user to temporarily ignore the effects of injury. The basic power has one way to commit Force dice: [BR]- When the character suffers a Critical Injury with a severity no greater than [B]Easy difficulty[b], the character may activate Endure as an out-of-turn incidental, committing a Force die. While the Force die remains committed, the character ignores the effects of that Critical Injury. This means they do not apply any results from the Critical Injury or add +10 to further rolls on the Critical Injury Result table while the Force die remains committed. (The injury can still be healed.) When this ongoing effect ends, the character suffers all effects of the Critical Injury (unless it has been treated).

ForceAbility.Name: Enhance Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: Enhance allows Force users to perform athletic feats beyond the original scope of their natural abilities. The basic power has one way of spending Force points: [BR]- When making an Athletics check, the user may roll an [B]Enhance power check[b] as part of the pool. The user may spend a Force point to gain a success or [ADVANTAGE] result (their choice) on the check. (Remember, this counts as a normal Force power check in every way—it is simply combined with the overall skill check.)

ForceAbility.Name: Farsight Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: In its most basic form, Farsight allows the Force user to see in situations in which normal visual detection would be impossible, such as in total darkness or heavily obscuring smoke. Using Farsight, it is even possible for those without eyes or have lost their sight to see with perfect vision. [BR]- The user may spend a Force point to see out to medium range for the remainder of the round (or one minute in narrative time), and can see everything most sentients can see on a well-lit day. This functions even if the user normally can't see due to darkness or blindness.

ForceAbility.Name: Foresee Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The most basic form of Foresee allows the character to look into the Force to see vague hints of their near future. These hints may be blurry visual images, brief samples of sound, or simple emotions. The basic power has one way of spending Force points:[P]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to gain vague hints of events to come in the next day of their own, personal future. The basic power cannot see further than one day.

ForceAbility.Name: Heal/Harm Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: Unlike many other Force powers, Heal/Harm has a basic power that can be used in two distinct ways (to heal or to harm). Heal allows the Force user to treat their comrades' injuries, while Harm lets them drain the life from their foes. When a character purchases the basic power Heal/Harm, they gain access to both Heal and Harm. Each time a character uses the basic power, they must choose whether they are using Heal or Harm, and they receive only the effects associated with their choice. Each upgrade a character purchases improves both Heal and Harm, but some improve each power in a different way.[P][B]Heal (Light Side Force User Only)[b][P]The basic power for Heal lets a character mend wounds with a simple touch. Heal can only be used by light side Force-sensitive characters. The basic power has one way to spend Force points: [BR]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to heal a number of wounds equal to their Intellect on one engaged living creature (including themself). This counts as a use of a stimpack on the affected target. This means a single target may only benefit from five uses of Heal over a twenty-four-hour period and their uses of Heal also count against the limit on uses of stimpacks (and vice versa). The user may not activate this multiple times.[P][B]Harm[b][P]The basic power for Harm lets a character drain the very life from a target with a touch. The basic power has one way to spend Force points:[P]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to inflict a number of wounds (ignoring soak) equal to the Force user's Intellect on one engaged living creature. The user gains 1 Conflict. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Imbue Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The basic power of Imbue can be used in one way: to boost the characteristics of one nearby ally. The basic power has one way to spend Force points: [BR]- The user may spend two Force points to increase one of another engaged character's characteristics by 1 (to a maximum of 6) until the end of the Force user's next turn. This can only be used once per target per encounter. If the user used a dark point to generate a Force point, the target increases a second characteristic by 1 (to a maximum of 6) until the end of the user's next turn, but both the Force user and the target suffer 3 strain.

ForceAbility.Name: Influence Basic Power

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The most basic form of Influence does not allow the Force user to guide or shape the thoughts of others. They can merely strain their mind, inflicting stress and exhaustion. The basic power has one effect that can be triggered multiple times on the same or different targets:[P]- The user spends a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to stress the mind of one living target they are engaged with, inflicting 1 strain. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the strain inflicted by one each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of targets affected by an amount equal to the user's Presence multiplied by the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: Spend two Force points increase the number of targets affected by an amount equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to increase the maximum encumbrance of the facsimile by an amount equal to twice the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. (If using the Mastery upgrade, this upgrade increases the silhouette of the summoned creature by an amount equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased, instead.) This may not be activated multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to exclude a number of engaged characters equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased from being affected by this power. The Force user may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: The character can use Endure to affect allies at short range. The character must commit a Force die as normal, and the Critical Injury must be of a severity that Endure could affect normally. The ongoing effect ends if the character stops committing a Force die or if the distance between the character and the ally increases beyond short range for any reason.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to affect engaged allies with the power as well as themself. This increases the number of people affected by the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: The Magnitude upgrade improves both Heal and Harm in the same way. Spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of targets affected by an amount equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of minds being affected equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of targets affected by a number up to the user's Presence multiplied by the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of targets affected by an amount equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time. However, remember that the user must still spend Force points to activate the power's actual effects.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: The Magnitude upgrade has different effects for Protect and for Unleash.[P]- [B]Protect:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of targets affected by the power by an amount equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The Force user may still only reduce damage from one hit among all affected targets. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time. [BR]- [B]Unleash:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to inflict one additional hit on a number of targets engaged with the original target equal to the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. These hits deal the same damage as the initial hit. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of additional hits by this number each time. Each target may only be hit once.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to gain one additional helpful detail per rank of Magnitude about the location, direction, or path of the target when using the basic power to search for it. These details can include short flashes of phenomena including sights, sounds, smells, landmarks, or even brief visions, as determined by the GM. For instance, if the basic power reveals that the user's quarry was headed in the direction of the Yavin system, the GM might have this upgrade provide the user with an image of light falling through the leaves of large trees—giving the user an important hint as to which planet (or moon) in that system the target has chosen as a hiding place.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of targets affected by the number of Magnitude upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Magnitude
ForceAbility.Description: When performing a Warde's Foresight power check as part of an Initiative check, the user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to add an automatic success result or [ADVANTAGE] result to the first check one ally within short range makes this encounter (after the Initiative check). The user may activate this multiple times, adding additional automatic success results or [ADVANTAGE] results to that ally or another ally's check each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Manipulate Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user shapes machine components on a molecular level, allowing better crafting and repairing of items.[P]The Force user may spend a Force point to cause one vehicle or starship they are engaged with to recover one system strain. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the system strain recovered by one each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: When the user activates this power without spending Force points generated from dark point results, add a light point to all other Force power checks made within this power's area of effect for the duration of the power.[P]When the user activates this power without spending Force points generated from light point results, add a dark point to all other Force power checks made within this power's area of effect for the duration of the power.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: If no Dark points were used to generate a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) the user may choose one skill; while under the effects of the power, each affected character counts as having the same number of ranks in the chosen skill as the affected character with the most ranks in that skill. If any Dark points were used to generate a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) on this check, each target affected must make an [B]Easy difficulty Discipline check[b] if they wish to resist obeying any orders given by the user as part of this power.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: When the user is making a [B]Bind power check[b], if the check was not already opposed, the user may roll an [B]opposed Discipline versus Discipline check[b] as part of the pool. To activate this upgrade, they must generate enough Force points to activate the power [I]and[i] must succeed at the opposed check. If no Dark points were used to generate Force points, the target is also staggered until the end of the user's next turn. If the user succeeds and used any Dark points to generate Force points on this check, the target immediately suffers a Critical Injury with a +10 to the roll per Force point spent on the check.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: Conjuring items is a strange use of the Force known only to a few, such as the Nightsisters of Dathomir, and for good reason: knowledge of such conjuration can lead to far darker paths than mere duplication of physical things. Masters of the ability can give false life to entire living beings or, far more horrifying, raise corpses to fight like abominable puppets on foul strings. Only the greatest of Nightsisters have ever been known to master such an ability to this extent.[P]The Force user may spend three Force points to create a facsimile of a living creature of silhouette 1 or smaller instead of an object. This creature uses the profile of a living minion NPC of the Force user's choice, obeys the will of the Force user, and ceases to exist at the end of the Force user's next turn. The Force user may spend a maneuver to direct their facsimile, allowing it to perform an action and a maneuver.[P]If, however, the user has a corpse of a silhouette 1 or smaller available, they can instead animate it, bringing it to false life and gaining 7 Conflict in the process. This abomination uses the profile of the deceased being, obeys the will of the Force user, and ceases to be animated at the end of the Force user's next turn. The Force user may spend a maneuver to direct the corpse, allowing it to spend an action and a maneuver.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: The Mastery upgrade has different effects for Ebb and Flow.[P]- [B]Ebb:[b] Once per session, if a character suffered at least 5 strain from a single use of this power, the Force user may choose to add an automatic [DESPAIR] result to that character's next skill check. [BR]- [B]Flow:[b] Once per session, if the Force user healed at least 5 strain from a use of this power, the Force user may choose to add an automatic [TRIUMPH] to their next skill check.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: When the character activates Endure, they may make an Endure power check instead of committing a Force die as normal. An Endure power check is a Discipline check with a difficulty equal to the severity of the Critical Injury, to which the character may add Force dice up to their Force rating. If the character succeeds on the check and generates Force points equal to the number of [DIFFICULTY] dice in the severity of the Critical Injury, the Critical Injury is not suffered.[P]An Endure power check cannot prevent a Critical Injury result of Dead.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend two Force points. The user now can see as though from a spot within close range (planetary scale) of the user's body. If the user is on the surface of a world, this distance can be a vertical altitude in the air as well as along the surface; if in space this can be in any direction. This effectively moves the character's personal point of view far away from the location of the user's body, allowing a viewpoint as if controlling a remote viewing mechanism.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: The Mastery upgrade has different effects for Heal and for Harm.[P]- [B]Heal:[b] The user may spend four Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to resuscitate one target of the power who died since the end of the Force user's last turn. Immediately remove the Critical Injury or other effect that killed the target. The Force user can only activate this once per session. Note that in this case, the user is pulling the target back from the brink of death, not actually bringing them back to life. [BR]- [B]Harm:[b] When this power kills a sentient living target, the user may restore to life an engaged character who died this encounter. Immediately remove the Critical Injury or other effect that killed the target. The user and the character revived this way each gain 7 Conflict. Note that this Conflict gain is only for the perversion of nature that is returning a soul to its body after its time has come, and not for any associated acts of evil, such as killing an innocent to do it, which may generate additional Conflict. The user may only activate this once per session.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user increases characteristics boosted by this power by 2 (to a maximum of 7) instead of 1 (to a maximum of 6).

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: When performing a Manipulate power check as part of a Mechanics skill check, the user may spend two Force points when using the power to gain a [TRIUMPH] result on the check. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: Some Force users possess the ability to project not just a single vision upon those around them, but to create incredibly complex illusionary realms or vast swarms of howling terrors to intimidate their enemies. Though few Force users ever achieve such heights of power over the senses of others, those who do may spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to increase the number of objects obscured or illusions created by an amount up to the user's Cunning plus their ranks in Deception. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of objects hidden or altered or illusions created by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: The Mastery upgrade has different effects for Protect and for Unleash.[P]- [B]Protect:[b] This upgrade represents gaining the clarity of mind required to let energy and aggression flow harmlessly through the Force user and back to their attackers. A light side Force user may spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to reflect all attacks that would be reduced to 0 damage (before soak) by this power back upon their sources. Each attack reflected this way hits the attacker for the amount of damage it would have dealt to the user (before the deduction for Protect). [BR]- [B]Unleash:[b] This upgrade represents mastering the ultimate dark side technique, the dreaded Force lightning. If the user is a dark side Force user, they may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to reduce the attack's critical rating to 1.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user scans the target with their mind, following the flow of energy to the flaw that will be the enemy's undoing. The Force user makes a Force check as an action and chooses an enemy they can perceive. If they spend at least three Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]), the user adds one automatic [TRIUMPH] result to each combat check they make against the target until the end of the encounter. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Mastery
ForceAbility.Description: The user may choose an enemy within short range and attempt to disrupt that foe's use of the Force. The user makes a [B]Suppress power check[b] and rolls an [B]opposed Discipline vs. Discipline check[b] as part of the pool. If the user spends two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) and succeeds on the opposed Discipline check, the user causes the target Force user to immediately uncommit all committed Force dice and immediately end all ongoing effects of Force powers, Force talents, and any other effects that required committed Force dice. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Misdirect Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The Misdirect power allows the user to manipulate the senses of others, beguiling their targets so that they can hide people and objects in plain sight or impose sensory illusions on those targets. The basic power has one way to spend Force points:[P]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to deceive the senses of a living target at short range or closer. The target does not perceive one object or being a silhouette 1 or lower that is within their line of sight until the beginning of the Force user's next turn. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Move Basic Power

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: At its most basic, Move allows the Force user to move small objects that are near them. It has one basic effect:[P]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to move one object of silhouette 0 that is within short range up to their maximum range. The default maximum range is short range. The user may not activate this multiple times..

ForceAbility.Name: Number
ForceAbility.Description: Spend two Force points to conjure one additional facsimile of the same type as the first per Magnitude upgrade purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of facsimiles conjured by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Protect/Unleash Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: Unlike many other Force powers, Protect/Unleash has a basic power that can be used in two very different ways. A character who purchases the basic power Protect/Unleash gains access to both Protect and Unleash. Each time a character uses the basic power, they must choose whether to use Protect or Unleash and receives only the effects associated with that choice. Each upgrade a character purchases improves both Protect and Unleash, but some improve each power in a different way.[P][B]Protect[b][P]The basic power for Protect lets a Force user shield themself or an ally against oncoming energy attacks. A dark side Force user cannot use Protect to defend allies (they can only use it to protect themself]. The basic power has one way to spend Force points: [BR]- The user chooses themself or one ally they are currently engaged with and makes a [B]Protect power check[b] and rolls an [B]Average difficulty Discipline check[b] as part of the pool. To raise this Force barrier, they must spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to activate the power and they must succeed on the Discipline check. Once the power is activated, if the target of the power suffers a hit from a blaster shot, Force power, lightsaber, or other energy attack before the beginning of the user's next turn, the character may reduce damage by an amount equal to their Willpower characteristic plus the number of success results scored on the Discipline check. The power may only reduce damage from one hit during its duration. Dark side Force users may only protect themselves with Protect. The user may not activate this multiple times.[P][B]Unleash[b][P]The basic power for Unleash lets a character blast an enemy with a surge of manifest emotion. The basic power has one way to spend Force points:[P]- The Force user makes a [B]Unleash power check[b] and rolls a ranged attack as part of the pool. The attack uses an [B]Average difficulty Discipline check[b] instead of the normal difficulty for ranged attacks, and only succeeds if the user also spends two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]). The attack has a range of short, a base damage equal to the user's Willpower, and a critical rating of 4. The user gains 1 Conflict. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend two Force points to increase the range of the affected area by a number of range bands equal to Range upgrades purchased. The Force user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the maximum range at which the Force user can affect targets through this power by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to increase the maximum range at which the Force user can affect targets with this power by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to increase the range at which the facsimile can be conjured and sustained by one. This can be activated multiple times, increasing the range by one each time (to a maximum of extreme range).

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend two Force points to affect all other characters at short range with this power, instead of affecting all other engaged characters.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The range at which the character can use Endure to affect allies increases to medium. The ongoing effect ends if the distance between characters increases beyond medium for any reason.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to increase the maximum range the user can jump by the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may not activate this multiple times. Remember that the user must still spend Force points to activate the power's actual effects.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point to increase the power's range by one range band equal to Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the range at which they can affect their allies with this power by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The Range upgrade improves both Heal and Harm in the same way. Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the maximum range at which the Force user can affect targets with this power by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend two Force points to increase the range of this power by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The Force user may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Range

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the range at which the character can tough minds by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The user may spend a Force point to increase the power's range by a number of personal range bands equal to Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the maximum range at which the Force user can affect targets with this power by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the maximum range at which the user can move objects by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time. However, remember the user must still spend Force points to activate the power's actual effects.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: The Range upgrade improves both Protect and Unleash in the same way. Spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to increase the maximum range at which the Force user can affect targets with this power by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the range at which the character senses living things by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the maximum range at which the Force user can affect targets with this power by a number of range bands equal to Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Range
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the power's range by a number of range bands equal to the number of Range upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the range by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Seek Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: Seek's basic power allows Force users to find faraway things and to shatter sensory tricks that might hide their quarry. The basic power has two ways to spend Force points:[P]- The user may spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to gain insight into the general location or direction of a person or object that they know about, regardless of its current distance from them. The user may not activate this multiple times. [BR]- The user may make an [B]Average difficulty Vigilance check[b] with the power check to see through all sensory misdirections confronting them, whether these come from technology or more esoteric sources. This power works against tricks such as cloaking fields, holograms, Force illusions, and even physical disguises, at the GM's discretion, but has no direct effect on spoken or written lies. To successfully see past the deception, the character must spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to activate the power [I]and[i] must succeed on the Average difficulty [B]Vigilance check[b] (or [B]opposed Vigilance versus Discipline check[b] if illusions are being created by another Force user). If the user succeeds, their supernatural senses pierce the falsehoods, letting them perceive the truth they conceal.

ForceAbility.Name: Sense Basic Power

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: Sense's basic power allows the Force user to sense the living Force interacting with the world around them. This allows them to perceive life and read emotions. The basic power has two ways to spend Force points:[P]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to sense all living things within short range of themself (including animals and sentient beings). The user may not activate this multiple times. [BR]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to sense the current emotional state of one living target with whom they are engaged. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to select a number of targets equal to the number of Strength upgrades purchased; these targets ignore the power's effects. The Force user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of targets that can ignore this power's effects by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: Spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to add one additional success result to all affected characters' checks. The user may activate this multiple times, adding one additional success result to all checks each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point to disorient the target for a number of rounds equal to the number of Strength upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of rounds by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user can spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to pick out a number of specific details from their vision equal to the number of Strength upgrades purchased. The use may activate this multiple times, recalling more details each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: The Strength upgrade has different effects for Heal and for Harm.[P]- [B]Heal:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to heal 1 additional wound on the target per rank of Strength purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of wounds healed by this number each time. [BR]- [B]Harm:[b] The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to inflict 1 additional wound per rank of Strength purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the number of wounds inflicted by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: If no dark points were used to generate a Force point, the Force user decreases all Critical Injuries that the target suffers and the target inflicts by 10 per Strength upgrade purchased. If no light points were used to generate a Force point, the Force user increases all Critical Injuries that the target suffers and the target inflicts by 10 per Strength upgrade purchased.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: When stressing the mind of a target, the Force user inflicts 2 strain instead of 1.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: When using this power to cause a target to recover strain or system strain or heal wounds, the user may spend a Force point to cause the target to recover one additional strain, system strain, or heal one additional wound per Strength upgrade. This may be activated multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: Spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to increase the silhouette of the object able to be obscured or the illusion created by 1 per rank of Strength purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the silhouette they can affect by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the maximum silhouette of objects a character can move by a number equal to the number of Strength upgrades purchased. The user may activate this multiple times, increasing the silhouette of the objects they can move by this number each time.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: The Strength upgrade improves both Protect and Unleash. Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to increase the damage reduced by Protect by 1 per Strength upgrade for this use, or spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to add 1 damage per Strength upgrade to the base damage of Unleash for this attack. The user may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to completely eliminate one Force-based illusion per rank of Strength purchased instead of merely seeing through it when using the basic power. Force illusions banished this way stop working against all targets they previously affected and vanish like mist in the sun. The user can activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength

Sources.Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook

ForceAbility.Description: When using Sense's ongoing effects, the user may upgrade one additional die.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: Spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to add additional an automatic [FAILURE] result equal to the number of Strength upgrades purchased to hostile Force power checks targeting characters affected by Suppress. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength
ForceAbility.Description: Spend two Force points ([FORCEPOINT][FORCEPOINT]) to gain a [BOOST] die equal to Strength upgrades purchased on the user's next check against the target (or directly involving the target, in the case of a non-combat check). The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength - Ignore Death
ForceAbility.Description: The character can use Endure to affect a Critical Injury of Dead until the end of the current encounter (or until they stop committing a Force die). A Critical Injury of Dead cannot be treated or healed.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength - Increase Severity
ForceAbility.Description: The character increases the severity of Critical Injuries they can affect using Endure by one per Strength upgrade purchased.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength: Failure/Success
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to increase the success result added to their checks before the end of their next turn by 1, or increase the [FAILURE] result added to engaged characters before the end of their next turn by 1. The Force user may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength: Strain
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to increase the strain healed or inflicted by this power by 1. The Force user may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Strength: Threat/Advantage
ForceAbility.Description: The Force user may spend a Force point to increase the [ADVANTAGE] result added to their checks before the end of their next turn by 1, or increase the [THREAT] result added to engaged characters before the end of their next turn by 1. The Force user may activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Suppress Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: The basic power of Suppress can be used in one way: to create a projective bubble around the Force user that dampens the effects of other Force powers meant to harm the user and nearby allies. The basic power has one way to spend Force points:[P]The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to extend a dampening field around themselves that shields them and all allies in short range. Until the end of the user's next turn, any hostile Force user who makes a skill check as part of a Force power check against the user or any affected ally add an automatic [FAILURE] result to the results. The user may not activate this multiple times.

ForceAbility.Name: Warde's Foresight Basic Power
ForceAbility.Description: Warde's Foresight differs from many other prophetic abilities in that it focuses very narrowly on a specific person. At the most basic level, it observes not the future of the cosmos but the fate of a particular individual. However, even these hints that Warde's power of prophecy grants are only likelihoods. The future is volatile, shifting with the choices of individuals. Even the decision whether or not to act on these visions of possible futures can alter results they foreshadowed. The basic power has one way to spend Force points:[P]- The user may spend a Force point ([FORCEPOINT]) to gain hints about what an individual within short range is likely to do in the near future. In structured gameplay, this knowledge does not typically extend beyond the end of the current encounter.
